item.title: Saturday, September 19: Military AI Near-Miss, iPhone 18 Pro Launch, and Meta Muse
item.description:
An AI hallucination nearly triggers a United States military interception of a Chinese vessel, while Apple launches the iPhone 18 Pro lineup worldwide. Plus, Meta expands its Muse desktop agent to Mac, and California pushes for mandated AI kill switches.

Stories covered:

  • AI Hallucination of Chinese Nuclear Components Nearly Triggered US Military Attack (Ars Technica)
  • Apple Launches iPhone 18 Pro and Apple Watch Series 12 as Foldable 'iPhone Duo' Previews Emerge (9to5Mac)
  • Meta's New Muse AI Agent Launches on Mac, Overtaking ChatGPT in App Store (TechCrunch)
  • California Governor Gavin Newsom Pushes for Mandated AI 'Kill Switches' (The Verge)
  • FCC Allows Gulf Sovereign Wealth Funds to Acquire 49.5% Stake in Paramount-Warner Bros. (Ars Technica)
  • FBI and Coast Guard Board Hacked Oil Tankers Heading to US Coast After Systems Compromised (TechCrunch)
  • Anthropic Establishes Physical Biology Lab in San Francisco to Conduct Wet-Lab Experiments (TechCrunch)
  • Google Bypasses AOSP to Introduce Proprietary APIs in Android 17 (Hacker News)
item.itunes:summary: An AI hallucination nearly triggers a United States military interception of a Chinese vessel, while Apple launches the iPhone 18 Pro lineup worldwide. Plus, Meta expands its Muse desktop agent to Mac, and California pushes for mandated AI kill switches.
